replacement.evidence_ref: decision 463295d5 — Joe approves Drive retirement across all dependency classes
replacement.verified: bin/nightly.sh refuses every remaining Drive projection on the normal path. Exercised live 2026-08-22: 13 steps logged BLOCKED and none touched Drive. Now ONE, and every step that left did so for a recorded reason rather than by being bypassed. The exports gained a canonical destination (CARR OneDrive, decision bdbb7441). The section index and the system graph were found already reading the store and writing inside the repository, refusing only because the wrapper still called them Drive projections; both were run on the normal path first and exited 0. Four retired outright because what they acted on is gone: cutover readiness verified compiled-rules markdown the cutoff retired, the vault drift watch at both ends guards a vault with no writers and no tracked files left, and the settings mirror had already declared itself retired in its own header with config-as-code owning the hooks block. The portability mirror joined them on 2026-08-22, repointed to the same OneDrive root as the exports; it wrote to two places and only the Drive half had died, so a live second copy under out/mirror had gone quiet with it. Verified by running it: 234 markdown documents, 36 tables, 52,809 rows into OneDrive. It carries a SEPARATE unresolved blocker that repointing does not touch — the step names CARR_DB_BACKUP_URL, which is absent from this Mac's credential file and is not among the two database URLs the routine boundary passes to children, so it will report NOT CONFIGURED and skip until that credential is provisioned. The remaining five still refuse: upstream corroborate, corpus push, the consumer boards, lead promote, and the graph. The consumer boards and lead promote left on 2026-08-23, and neither needed a destination or a grant: lib/record_sources.pool_reach returned failure as soon as its elevated probe raised, so the exporter view path below it was reachable only when no elevated DSN was configured at all. The routine boundary passes both credentials, the jobs one is refused on candidate_pool and on v_export_pool_all, and the exporter one reads the view with 9,870 rows — so a working path was skipped and reported as a privilege problem. Verified under the boundary's exact two credentials: lead board 9,868 leads, deal room 172 deals, lead promote 11 candidates, all exit 0. The remaining three refuse: upstream corroborate, corpus push, and the graph. The corpus push left on 2026-08-23 without weakening the retirement: the tool refuses vault-rooted rows itself, on retirement rather than on reachability, because the Drive mount still resolves here and a reachability probe would have rewritten retired renders back into the vault. Twelve home-rooted rows addressing ~/.claude/skills now push on the normal path; forty-two vault rows are held and printed with their reason, and move only inside an opened recovery envelope. Guarded by ops/corpus-push-root-split-selftest.py, which asserts both halves because either alone is satisfied by a version that breaks the other. The remaining two refuse: upstream corroborate and the graph. The graph left on 2026-08-23. Its label said it derived from exported files and it does not: both halves read the store and write out/Graph in the repository. One raw disk read had been left behind — a listing of DNA/Clients/prospects used to recover the casing of hand-written client dossiers — and that directory was retired with the vault, so the listing raised and took the graph with it. The client records name those files themselves (23 of 201), so the map is built from the rows. Verified under the routine boundary's credentials: 77 nodes, 1,895 edges, 178 client nodes, exit 0. Only upstream corroborate still refuses, and it waits on an external listing intake rather than on anything in this repository. ONE remains, and it is not a Drive problem at all — its seam name said 'record-backed pre-entity-watch document destination', which describes the output and sent two readers hunting for somewhere to write. Corrected 2026-08-23. Upstream corroborate joins seven weak signal families and needs weight 3 across at least two classes before it names anyone. Those seven files are built by five scripts under pipelines/radar and, checked that day, not one of the five is called by the chain, by ops/ or by run.sh. They consume externally acquired datasets — a quarterly CMS provider-enrolment extract, a licensing file filtered in browser memory so the raw statewide file never touches disk — and both DELETE their input immediately after running, because it identifies real practitioners. That discard rule is a deliberate privacy control. Making this step nightly is therefore a decision about acquiring and retaining other people's data, not a wiring task, and it stays refused until someone with the authority to answer that does. HOW IT REFUSES CHANGED ON 2026-08-23, and what it refuses did not. Until then a refused projection was EXECUTED so that it could refuse: the step launched bin/routine-canonical-seam-refusal.sh under the step wrapper, that process exited 69, and step() printed BLOCKED into out/nightly.log. The sentence was the whole product and the process was overhead — a launch, a wall clock and a ledger row to say something already known before the chain started, every night for weeks, in the same word a real break would use. It is now a TOMBSTONE: the step is gated out before it runs, and one log line names what is missing and what would reopen it. Nothing about the refusal itself moved — the drive_projection callsites are unchanged, the recovery envelope still runs the real command, and this row's normal_path is still normal_path_refuses_missing_canonical_seams. A reader looking for the word BLOCKED in the nightly log will not find it, and should read the receipt line (blocked=N tombstoned=N timed_out=N) instead.
